rounds.text: Refex Renewables & Infrastructure Ltd is experiencing a powerful operational turnaround that the market has not yet priced in, with recent results scoring a maximum 100 out of 100 driven by a stellar 58% year-on-year surge in net profit and 33% year-on-year sales growth [E41, E43, E45]. This fundamental acceleration is matched by stellar capital efficiency, highlighted by a towering Return on Equity of 52.46% that vastly outperforms the sector benchmark of 10.51% [E8]. Furthermore, the business is demonstrating robust cash generation, pulling in Rs 16 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 10 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026, while debtor days have notably improved from 29.0 to 21.7 days [E26, E27, E36]. Operational execution is also tightening at the margins, with quarterly operating margin increasing to 53% in June 2026, supported by a four-quarter trend of expanding margins [E22, E24]. Conceded: [E13] compounded sales growth over 3 years is -5%, [E17] compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months is -8%, [E20] compounded share price growth over 1 year is -53%, [E28] current ratio stands at 0.30x with borrowings at Rs 487 Cr, and [E39] contingent liabilities total Rs 160 Cr. Dismissing this active turnaround based on stale sentiment ignores clear evidence of accelerating momentum [E45].

Refex Renewables & Infrastructure Ltd carries heavy balance sheet distress, highlighted by a current ratio of just 0.30x where current liabilities severely exceed current assets [E28]. This precarious liquidity is compounded by massive borrowings of Rs 487 Cr as of March 2026, which have grown from Rs 473 Cr a year earlier [E29], and a low interest coverage ratio flagged directly as a negative [E37]. Furthermore, the company struggles with foundational profitability and returns, evidenced by a weak ROCE of 3.3% [E11] and a dismal ROA of -7.46% against a sector benchmark of 4.91% [E7]. Top-line erosion remains a persistent structural hurdle, demonstrated by negative compounded sales growth over both 5 years (-2%) and 3 years (-5%) [E12, E13, E38], alongside a 5-year compounded profit contraction of -14% [E15]. Market sentiment has aggressively repriced these underlying fundamental risks, plunging the stock down -53% over the past year [E20] to sit merely 26% of the way up its 52-week range [E4], while looming contingent liabilities of Rs 160 Cr [E39] further threaten financial stability. Conceded: [E8], [E22], [E24], [E26], [E27].

While the bear highlights a low current ratio of 0.30x [E28], rising borrowings of Rs 487 Cr [E29], and low interest coverage [E37], these balance sheet pressures completely overlook the tangible cash generation occurring on the ground, with positive operating cash flow of Rs 16 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 10 Cr in March 2026 [E26, E27]. The bear points to long-term sales contraction (-2% over 5 years) [E12, E38] and profit contraction (-14% over 5 years) [E15], but ignores that the company is currently pivoting hard with TTM sales growth recovering to 8% [E14], recent quarterly sales jumping +33% YoY [E41], and net profit surging +58% YoY [E43]. The bear cites a weak ROCE of 3.3% [E11] and a 52-week range sitting at 26% [E4], yet ignores a stellar ROE of 52.46% massively outperforming the sector benchmark of 10.51% [E8], alongside four consecutive quarters of increasing operating margins reaching 53% in June 2026 [E22, E24]. Conceded: [E7], [E13], [E16], [E20], [E39].

The bull’s reliance on recent cash flow [E26, E27] ignores the structural insolvency signaled by a current ratio of 0.30x, which confirms that current liabilities vastly exceed current assets [E28]. While the bull highlights a pivot in growth [E41, E43], this short-term momentum fails to offset the long-term decay evidenced by a 5-year sales contraction of -2% [E12, E38] and a 5-year profit contraction of -14% [E15]. The claim that ROE is stellar [E8] is misleading when the company’s ROCE remains a dismal 3.24% compared to the sector benchmark of 12.53% [E9, E11], indicating that the business is failing to generate adequate returns on its capital base. Furthermore, the bull’s focus on margin expansion [E22, E24] ignores the reality of a low interest coverage ratio [E37] and rising debt levels of Rs 487 Cr [E29], which threaten the sustainability of any operational gains. The company also carries significant contingent liabilities of Rs 160 Cr [E39], creating a substantial risk profile that the bull’s narrative of a "turnaround" fails to account for. Conceded: [E14], [E22], [E26], [E27], [E41], [E43].
